# Le050 — Unicode characters in STEP export silently dropped

<!-- Auto-generated; edit `STEP_PROBLEM_CATALOG.md` instead. -->

## Description

A document name contains non-ASCII characters (Cyrillic, CJK, Greek). STEP exporter ASCII-encodes the file body but does not escape non-ASCII via `\X2\…\X0\`; the characters are emitted as raw bytes that cause downstream readers to mis-decode or reject.

## Reproducer recipe

Document with name `'Тест'` (Cyrillic). Writer emits raw bytes `'\xD0\xA2\xD0\xB5\xD1\x81\xD1\x82'` in an Ed.2-declared file — illegal under Ed.2.

## Expected kernel behavior

writer escapes non-ASCII via the edition-appropriate directive (`\X2\` for Ed.2, raw UTF-8 for Ed.3 with proper FILE_DESCRIPTION declaration).

## Notes

**See also**: Le022, Le001. Provenance tier: requires-sibling-pair — bytes alone cannot demonstrate the writer-side dropping; the defect is the differential between the in-memory document name and the bytes the writer emits. Demonstrating this requires both the producer-input state (document with non-ASCII name) and the corrupted output it produces.
